## Basis

This report sets out the design basis for a distillation column that is intended to separate a key component from a liquid feed stream. The design throughput of the column is 29 t per day, and the separation duty that the column is required to achieve corresponds to 94% of the key component. It has been specified that all wetted parts of the column are to be manufactured from 316L stainless steel, and this requirement is recorded here in the basis section for the avoidance of doubt. The composition of the feed is not fixed, since it depends on the operation of the upstream process units, and the design has therefore been developed on the basis of the least favourable composition that is expected to arise within the normal feed envelope, so that the required duty can be achieved under all anticipated conditions rather than under nominal conditions only. The feed is introduced to the column as a liquid at its boiling point, and no allowance has been made in the design for any flash vapour that might be present in the feed stream. The operating pressure of the column is determined by the condensation of the overhead vapour against the cooling medium that is available on the site, and represents a compromise between the ease with which the separation can be achieved and the duty that is imposed on the condenser. The products of the column are an overhead product enriched in the key component and a bottoms product depleted in it, and the two product qualities are complementary aspects of the single separation duty that has been specified. Heating is provided by steam in the reboiler, and cooling by the site cooling medium in the condenser and in the product coolers that are provided downstream of the column.

## Sizing

The sizing of the column has been carried out in a stepwise manner, beginning with the determination of the stage requirement and proceeding from there to the internal traffic and finally to the dimensions of the shell itself. The stage requirement has been estimated by means of a shortcut calculation based on the equilibrium behaviour of the key component relative to the remainder of the feed. This approach yields the minimum number of stages that would be required at total reflux, together with the minimum reflux ratio at which the specified separation could in principle be achieved, and the operating reflux ratio has then been selected at a level above the minimum, at the point where the additional cost of providing further stages ceases to be justified by the corresponding saving in energy consumption. The internal vapour and liquid traffic within the column follows from the reflux ratio and from the product rates, and it is by no means uniform along the height of the column, since the liquid rate changes at the point at which the feed is introduced. The diameter of the column has been determined by reference to flooding, the vapour velocity at the design throughput having been held below the flooding velocity by a suitable margin, and the height has been built up from the number of trays, the spacing between them, and the various disengaging and access allowances that are required at the top and at the bottom of the column. The pressure drop through the column has been estimated tray by tray and taken into account in establishing the conditions at the base of the column, where it influences the temperature at which the reboiler is required to operate.

## Materials

As recorded in the basis section of this report, the wetted parts of the column are to be manufactured from the stainless steel grade that is specified there, and this section of the report is concerned with the reasoning that supports that selection and with the associated requirements for fabrication. The grade in question has been selected on the basis of its resistance to corrosion by the feed and by both of the products, over the whole of the temperature range that is encountered within the column, from the condenser at the top to the reboiler at the base. The same grade has been adopted at those locations where the process fluids are at their most concentrated, notably in the reboiler circuit and in the bottoms line, since it is at these locations that the combination of concentration and temperature is at its most severe. A corrosion allowance has been included in the thickness of the pressure-containing parts, over and above the thickness that is required by the pressure design, and this allowance is intended to provide for metal loss over the life of the plant rather than to contribute to the strength of the equipment. Welding is to be carried out using qualified procedures and matching consumables, and welds in wetted service are to be subjected to examination over their full length. The materials of gaskets and bolting have been selected for compatibility with the fluids and temperatures at the joints concerned, and external parts of the column that are not wetted by the process, such as the support skirt and the access platforms, are to be manufactured from carbon steel protected by a suitable coating system. Thermal insulation is to be provided where heat losses from the column would otherwise be sufficient to disturb the operation of the unit.

## Risks

There are two significant items that remain open at the time this report is issued, and it should be clearly understood that neither of them is resolved by the contents of the report. The first of these items concerns the fouling of the column internals, and the second concerns the behaviour of the column under turndown conditions. So far as fouling is concerned, the feed to the column will inevitably bring with it whatever material the upstream units pass forward, and the reboiler, where temperatures are at their highest and where the least volatile constituents of the feed tend to accumulate, is the item of equipment that is most exposed to the formation of deposits. The consequences of fouling would include a progressive reduction in the heat transfer performance of the reboiler, with a corresponding increase in steam consumption, together with a possible deterioration in the hydraulic behaviour of the trays. Unfortunately, the rate at which fouling would be expected to develop on this particular feed is simply not known at the present time, and no measurements are available that would allow a reliable estimate to be made. The provisions that might be adopted in response, which include additional reboiler capacity, facilities for cleaning, and various on-line washing arrangements, remain under consideration, as does the question of where responsibility for the decision should rest. So far as turndown is concerned, the column has been sized for its design throughput, and its performance at substantially lower throughputs has not been established. At reduced vapour rates the liquid seal on the trays is progressively weakened and liquid may begin to weep through the tray perforations, with a consequent loss of separation efficiency. The extent to which the column can be turned down while continuing to meet its specified duty is therefore a matter that can only be settled by testing, and the operating range that is to be guaranteed, and the means by which it is to be demonstrated, remain open questions. It should also be noted that the two items are not independent of one another, since a fouled column may be expected to turn down less satisfactorily than a clean one.

## Basis

The column separates a key component from a liquid feed by distillation. The design throughput is 29 t per day, and the separation duty is 94% of the key component, recovered from the feed in the overhead product. All parts of the column in contact with the process fluids are of 316L stainless steel; the grade is stated here, in the basis, and the materials section works from this statement. The feed composition is not constant: it varies with the operation of the units upstream, and the design is set on the least favourable composition within the stated feed envelope, so that the column meets its duty across the envelope rather than at a single nominal analysis. The feed enters the column as a liquid at its boiling point at the column pressure, and the sizing takes no credit for flash vapour in the feed.

Operating pressure is set by the condensing side: the overhead vapour is condensed against the cooling medium available at the site, and the pressure is the lowest at which that condensation can be completed with the medium at its warmest expected state. A lower pressure eases the separation and raises the reflux and boil-up needed for it; the stated pressure is the balance point between the ease of separation and the duty of the condenser, and it is held fixed through the sizing. The bottoms product leaves the key component behind at the complementary level set by the duty: what the overhead recovers, the bottoms loses, and the two product specifications are the one duty stated from the two ends of the column. Utilities are steam for the reboiler and the site cooling medium for the condenser and the product coolers; no utility rate is fixed in the basis, since the rates follow from the sizing.

## Sizing

The sizing proceeds in three steps: the stage requirement, the internal traffic, and the shell dimensions that the traffic sets. The stage requirement is found by a shortcut calculation on the equilibrium of the key component against the remainder of the feed: the minimum stage count at total reflux, the minimum reflux for the specified separation, and an operating reflux set above the minimum by a margin that the economics of the trade-off between stages and energy supports. The operating point is chosen where the added cost of further stages no longer buys a worthwhile saving in reboiler duty, and that choice, rather than any rule stated in advance, fixes the number of stages the column is built with.

Internal traffic follows from the reflux and the products: the vapour rate is highest at the top of the column and the liquid rate changes at the feed stage, and both sections are sized on their own traffic rather than on a single average. The diameter is set by flooding: the vapour velocity at the design rate is held below the flooding velocity by a margin that leaves room for the feed envelope to move, and the same check is applied in both sections of the column. Tray spacing is set by the need to keep entrained liquid out of the vapour space above each tray and to give access for inspection, and the height of the column is the sum of the tray stack, the disengaging spaces at the top and bottom, and the feed and draw allowances. Pressure drop is accumulated tray by tray and checked against the pressure basis: the bottom temperature that the reboiler must reach depends on the pressure at the bottom, and a sizing that let the drop grow without check would move the reboiler duty with it.

## Materials

Wetted parts are the stainless steel specified in the basis section. The selection rests on the corrosion behaviour of the feed and of the two products across the full temperature range of the column, from the condenser at the top to the reboiler at the bottom: the grade named in the basis resists the process fluids at every point of that range, and no point in the column is left to a lesser material on the argument that its duty is milder. Where the fluids concentrate — in the reboiler, where the least volatile components accumulate, and in the bottoms line — the same grade is used, since concentration and temperature act together at exactly those points.

The corrosion allowance is held as a thickness margin on the pressure parts, additional to the thickness the pressure calculation requires; the allowance is a life provision, not a strength provision, and it is not available to be traded against the pressure thickness at any later revision of the design. Welding is by qualified procedures with matching consumables, and welds in wetted service are examined over their full length, since a weld whose composition departs from the parent metal is the point at which corrosion of an otherwise resistant system usually starts. Gasket materials are selected for the same fluids and the same temperature range as the pipework they seal, and bolting is of a grade compatible with the flanges it clamps. Non-wetted externals — the skirt, the platforms, the insulation cladding — are of carbon steel with a protective coating, and they have no process duty. Insulation is fitted where the column loses heat at a rate that would disturb the internal traffic, and it is clad against weather over its full height.

## Risks

Two items stand open at the issue of this report, and neither is resolved in it: fouling of the column internals, and the turndown behaviour of the column.

Fouling. The feed brings into the column whatever the upstream units pass forward, and the reboiler, where the fluids are hottest and the least volatile material collects, is the surface most exposed to deposit formation. A deposit on the reboiler surface reduces the heat transfer through it, and the column answers with a higher steam demand for the same separation; a deposit on the trays distorts the liquid distribution and narrows the operating range from the top. The rate at which fouling would develop on this feed is not known, no measurement of it exists in the design record, and the report states the exposure without assigning it a rate. The open questions are the provision to be made — spare reboiler capacity, a cleaning access arrangement, an on-line washing provision, or acceptance of a falling performance between shutdowns — and the party who owns the decision; both stand open.

Turndown. The column is sized at the design throughput, and its behaviour at rates well below that point is not established. On trays, a falling vapour rate weakens the seal of liquid on the tray and then lets liquid weep through the perforations, so contact on which the separation depends is lost progressively rather than at a single point. How far the column can be turned down while still meeting the separation duty is a measured question, not a calculated one on the present record. The operating range to be guaranteed, and the test by which it would be proved, stand open alongside the fouling provision, and the two items interact: a fouled column turns down worse than a clean one, and any turndown guarantee given before the fouling provision is settled would rest on the clean condition alone.
